mainTopic: Why both halves of דברים 21:16 are needed, and when a ruling may be relied on in practice
overview: This amud finishes the teaching of אבא חנן on the פסוק in דברים 21:16. ״והיה ביום הנחילו את בניו״ teaches that a father may choose which son inherits. ״לא יוכל לבכר״ teaches that he may not take away the בכור's double portion. Each half seems provable from the other by a קל וחומר, built on the fact that a פשוט inherits even ראוי while a בכור's double portion does not. The גמרא shows that each half is needed to block a wrong conclusion. The גמרא then rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. רבי זריקא and רבי אבא differ over whether רבי stated this as a rule or ruled it in a real case, which depends on whether a stated הלכה or a מעשה רב is the stronger source. A ברייתא teaches that one may act only on an explicit הלכה למעשה, and that one may not compare cases. רב אשי limits that ban on comparing to טריפות. The amud ends with רבי יוחנן's instruction to his students and רבא's instructions on handling a ruling of his that seems flawed, during his life and after his death.

steps.title: Why does the תורה need to say 'He may not make the firstborn'?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why the words ״לא יוכל לבכר״ are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the verse have to say: 'He may not make the son of the beloved wife the firstborn'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the תורה needed to write ״לא יוכל לבכר״. This question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה does not waste words, so every phrase should teach something. The question assumes that, without this phrase, we might have reached the opposite conclusion. The next step shows exactly how.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the verse need to say this?
He may not make [the beloved wife's son] the firstborn
Firstborn son, who receives a double portion

phrases.english: Why does the verse need to say:
'He may not make [the son of the beloved] the firstborn'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the analysis of why each half of the פסוק is needed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does ״לא יוכל לבכר״ add that we would not know otherwise?

steps.title: Without that phrase, a קל וחומר would let the father take away the בכור's share
steps.stepSummary: Since a father may give a פשוט's share to anyone, one might reason that he can surely take away a בכור's extra share. So the תורה says ״לא יוכל לבכר״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the verse says, 'On the day he gives his sons their inheritance,' a person might think this is simple logic. A regular son is the stronger heir, since he takes a share even of property that was only due to the father. Yet the תורה lets the father give the inheritance to whomever he wants. A firstborn is the weaker heir, since he gets no double share of such property. So surely the father could take the firstborn's extra share away! That is why the verse says, 'He may not make the firstborn.'
steps.whatsHappening: The answer: since ״והיה ביום הנחילו״ lets a father choose who inherits, one might use a קל וחומר to say he can also cancel the בכור's double portion. ״לא יוכל לבכר״ blocks that conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר compares the two kinds of heirs. A פשוט has the stronger right, because he even takes from ראוי, yet the father can still redirect his share. A בכור has the weaker right, because he gets no double portion from ראוי, so logic says the father should surely be able to redirect his extra share. The פסוק comes to say this logic is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: 'On the day he gives his sons their inheritance': the source that a father may choose which son inherits
Isn't this simple logic? (opening of a קל וחומר)
A regular son who is not the firstborn
Property due to the father but not yet in his hands when he died
Property the father already owned when he died
Is it not all the more so?

steps.confusionAlert: ״שהורע כחו״ does not mean a בכור gets less than his brothers. It means only that his EXTRA portion does not apply to ראוי, so in that one way his right is weaker than a פשוט's.

phrases.english: Because it is stated:
'Then it shall be, on the day he gives his sons their inheritance.'
phrases.notes: This is the earlier part of the same פסוק. It is read as letting the father choose which son inherits.

phrases.english: For one might have thought: isn't it simple logic?
If a regular son, whose power is stronger,
in that he takes from property due as from property already owned,
phrases.notes: In other words, he inherits even money that was owed to his father but not yet collected.

phrases.english: the Torah still gave the father permission
to give the inheritance to whomever he wants;
then a firstborn, whose power is weaker,
in that he does not take from property due as from property already owned,
is it not all the more so [that the father could take his share away]?
Therefore the verse says: 'He may not make [the beloved's son] the firstborn.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Without ״לא יוכל לבכר״, a קל וחומר from the פשוט would allow a father to cancel the בכור's double portion.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that a father cannot take away the בכור's double portion, even though he may redirect a פשוט's share.

steps.title: Then why is 'On the day he gives his sons their inheritance' needed?
steps.stepSummary: Now the question is turned around: if the תורה said only ״לא יוכל לבכר״, what does ״והיה ביום הנחילו״ add?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the verse say only 'He may not make the firstborn.' Why does it also need to say, 'On the day he gives his sons their inheritance'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the same kind of question about the other half of the פסוק. This sets up a reverse קל וחומר in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 explained ״לא יוכל לבכר״ by pointing to ״והיה ביום הנחילו״. Now the גמרא asks what we would lose if only ״לא יוכל לבכר״ were written. The goal is to show that each half is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let it say [only this]

phrases.english: Then let it say only 'He may not make the firstborn';
why does the verse need to say:
'Then it shall be, on the day he gives his sons their inheritance'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses the question of step 1 onto the other half of the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does ״והיה ביום הנחילו״ add if ״לא יוכל לבכר״ is written?

steps.title: Without it, a reverse קל וחומר would forbid redirecting a פשוט's share
steps.stepSummary: Since even the weaker בכור's share cannot be taken away, one might reason that the stronger פשוט's share surely cannot be either. The פסוק's answer comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: For one might think this is simple logic. A firstborn is the weaker heir, since he gets no double share of property that was only due to the father. Yet the תורה says, 'He may not make the firstborn,' so his share cannot be taken away. A regular son is the stronger heir, since he takes a share even of such property. So surely his share cannot be taken away either!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds the opposite קל וחומר. If even the weaker בכור's portion is protected, then surely the stronger פשוט's portion is protected too. This step sets up the conclusion that ״והיה ביום הנחילו״ is needed, which the next step gives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same comparison as in step 2, but running the other way. In step 2 the father's freedom over the פשוט was used to suggest freedom over the בכור. Here the protection of the בכור is used to suggest protection for the פשוט. That is why the תורה needs ״והיה ביום הנחילו״ to teach that the father does have freedom over a פשוט's share.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose power is weaker
Whose power is stronger
The תורה said

steps.whatToRemember: Each half of the פסוק blocks a קל וחומר. ״לא יוכל לבכר״ protects the בכור's double portion, and ״והיה ביום הנחילו״ lets the father redirect a פשוט's share. Neither could be learned from the other by logic.

phrases.english: For one might have thought: isn't it simple logic?
If a firstborn, whose power is weaker,
in that he does not take from property due as from property already owned,
still the Torah said: 'He may not make the firstborn' [so his share is protected];
then a regular son, whose power is stronger,
in that he takes from property due as from property already owned,
is it not all the more so [that his share cannot be taken away]?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 by laying out the reverse קל וחומר that the second part of the פסוק comes to block.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Without ״והיה ביום הנחילו״, a קל וחומר from the בכור would forbid a father from redirecting a פשוט's share.

steps.title: The verse gives the father permission to choose his heirs
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא completes its answer. The פסוק ״והיה ביום הנחילו את בניו״ is the real source that a father may leave his estate to whichever heir he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the verse says, "On the day he gives his sons their inheritance": the תורה gave the father permission to leave his estate to whomever he wants.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its answer from Step 4. Since ״לא יוכל לבכר״ cannot teach that a father may shift a פשוט's share, the תורה needed ״והיה ביום הנחילו״ to teach it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 showed that ״לא יוכל לבכר״ alone would make us think the stronger פשוט share is also locked. That is why a separate פסוק is needed. ״והיה ביום הנחילו״ teaches that the father controls how his estate is divided among his heirs, which is the view of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.

keyTerms.meaning: "The verse teaches": introduces the פסוק that settles the question
His giving of inheritance
Permission, authority
To give as an inheritance

steps.whatToRemember: Each פסוק teaches something the other cannot. ״לא יוכל לבכר״ means the בכור's extra share cannot be taken away. ״והיה ביום הנחילו״ means the father may give the rest of the estate to whichever heir he wants.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"Then it shall be, on the day he gives his sons their inheritance"
the Torah gave permission to the father
to give the inheritance to whomever he wants.
phrases.notes: This means whichever of his heirs he chooses. That is רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's view, which the next line rules on.

steps.triggerLanguage: תלמוד לומר והיה ביום הנחילו את בניו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in Step 4 by naming the פסוק that is needed
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״והיה ביום הנחילו״ is needed to teach that a father may leave his estate to any heir he chooses, since ״לא יוכל לבכר״ alone would imply even the פשוט's share is fixed.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of four names, רבי זריקא reports that רבי ruled the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זריקא said in the name of רבי אמי, in the name of רבי חנינא, in the name of רבי: the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the practical question and reports a ruling: the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is passed down through several generations of teachers, ending with רבי, who is רבי יהודה הנשיא. In practice, a father may leave his estate to whichever heir he chooses. רבי זריקא reports this as a stated rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה follows (this opinion)
"רבי" with no name added means רבי יהודה הנשיא
The תנא who holds a father may leave his estate to whichever heir he wants

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זְרִיקָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי
phrases.english: Rabbi Zerika said that Rabbi Ami said
that Rabbi Chanina said that Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: "רבי" on its own always means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: The halacha follows Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי זריקא אמר רבי אמי אמר רבי חנינא אמר רבי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the scriptural source to the practical ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, as a stated rule.

steps.title: רבי אבא: רבי ruled this in a real case
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא corrects רבי זריקא's report. What was said is that רבי "ruled" (הורה) in an actual case, not that he declared a general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to him: What was stated is "he ruled."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא corrects the way the ruling was reported. He says רבי gave this ruling for a real case that came before him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree on the outcome: the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. The only change is the form of the ruling. רבי זריקא reported a stated rule, while רבי אבא reports a decision given in an actual case. This sets up the next question about why that difference matters.

keyTerms.meaning: He ruled, meaning he gave a decision in a real case
It was said, it was stated

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אבא is not disagreeing about the הלכה itself. Both say the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. He is only correcting how the ruling was given.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to him:
"He ruled" is what was stated.
phrases.notes: He means רבי decided this in a real case that came before him, not just as a teaching.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה רבי אבא הורה איתמר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects the wording of the report in Step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the form of the report, not the הלכה itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי זריקא reported a general statement, but the original was a ruling in a practical case

steps.title: What is their disagreement really about?
steps.stepSummary: Since both agree on the הלכה, the גמרא asks what principle they actually disagree about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why it matters whether רבי stated the rule or ruled in a case. This question sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions lead to the same practical result. So the disagreement must be about something deeper: which kind of ruling counts as the stronger source.

keyTerms.meaning: "About what do they disagree?": asks for the root of a dispute

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the point behind רבי אבא's correction
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What underlying principle separates רבי זריקא's version from רבי אבא's version

steps.title: Stated rule versus actual case
steps.stepSummary: רבי זריקא holds that a stated הלכה is the stronger source. רבי אבא holds that a ruling in an actual case (מעשה רב) is stronger.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds that a stated הלכה is better; the other master holds that an actual case carries more weight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that they disagree over which type of ruling is stronger: a teaching stated as a rule, or a decision made in a real case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זריקא reports the ruling as a stated rule because he thinks that is the more authoritative form. רבי אבא insists it was a ruling in a real case because he holds מעשה רב: a real decision carries more weight. Each one is presenting the ruling in the form he considers stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: One master holds
Is preferable, is stronger
An actual case carries great weight

phrases.english: One master holds: a stated halacha is better,
and the other master holds: an actual case is greater.

steps.triggerLanguage: מר סבר הלכה עדיפא ומר סבר מעשה רב
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי זריקא holds that a stated הלכה is stronger. רבי אבא holds that a ruling in an actual case is stronger.

steps.title: You may not learn practical הלכה without being told it is for practice
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one may not learn practical הלכה from a stated teaching or from a case one saw, unless told explicitly that it is the הלכה for practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One does not learn הלכה from a statement of learning or from a case one saw, until he is told that this is the הלכה for practice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on the topic of the last step: when may a person rely on a teaching or a case to decide what to do?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither source works on its own. A teaching may be only theory, and a case may depend on details you did not see. Only an explicit statement that this is the practical הלכה lets you act on it.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught: introduces a ברייתא
One does not learn or derive
From a teaching stated in study
הלכה for actual practice

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One does not learn halacha

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מִפִּי תַלְמוּד, וְלֹא מִפִּי מַעֲשֶׂה,
phrases.english: not from a statement of learning, and not from a case,
until they tell him: this is the halacha for practice.

steps.triggerLanguage: תנו רבנן אין למדין הלכה לא מפי תלמוד ולא מפי מעשה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא on the strength of a stated rule versus an actual case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neither a stated teaching nor an observed case is enough for practice without an explicit statement that it is הלכה למעשה.

steps.title: Act on it, but do not stretch it to other cases
steps.stepSummary: If one asked and was told it is the practical הלכה, he may act on it, but he may not apply it to other cases that only look similar.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he asked and they told him it is the הלכה for practice, he may go and act on it, as long as he does not compare it to other cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues: once told explicitly, a person may act. It then adds a limit, telling him not to stretch the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once told explicitly, the person may rely on the ruling for that situation. The ברייתא then adds a limit: he may not compare it to other cases. The next steps question this limit, and רב אשי narrows it to cases of טריפות only.

keyTerms.meaning: He may go and act on it
As long as, provided that
That he not compare it to other cases

steps.whatToRemember: You may act on a ruling only after being told it is הלכה למעשה. The added limit, 'provided that he does not compare,' is explained in step 13 as applying only to טריפות.

phrases.english: If he asked and they told him it is halacha for practice,
he may go and act on it,
as long as he does not compare.

steps.triggerLanguage: שאל ואמרו לו הלכה למעשה ילך ויעשה מעשה ובלבד שלא ידמה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא: permission to act, plus a limit
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An explicit practical ruling may be followed, but only for its own case, without comparing it to others.

steps.title: How can we be told not to compare cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's line 'provided that he does not compare,' since comparing cases is the basic way the whole Torah is learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'provided that he does not compare' mean? We compare cases to each other throughout the entire תורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the last words of the ברייתא from step 11 and asks how they can be true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most הלכה is worked out by taking a case we know and applying it to a similar case we don't know. So a blanket rule against comparing cases seems to block normal learning. The גמרא needs a narrower meaning for the ברייתא's words.

keyTerms.meaning: Provided that, only on condition that
He will compare (one case to another)
We really do compare (cases to each other)

phrases.english: What does "provided that he does not compare" mean?
But the entire Torah, all of it,
we learn by comparing cases!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כׇּל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ דַּמּוֹיֵי מְדַמֵּינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the last clause of the ברייתא quoted in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's words 'provided that he does not compare.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Comparing cases is the normal way the whole Torah is learned, so a general ban on comparing cannot be right.

steps.title: The ban on comparing applies only to טריפות
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the ברייתא only forbids comparing cases in the area of טריפות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: this is what it means: provided that he does not compare one case of טריפות to another.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question by limiting the ברייתא to one specific area of הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In general comparing cases is fine. The ברייתא only means you may not take one injury that makes an animal a טריפה and stretch it to a similar-looking injury. This keeps normal Torah reasoning in place.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means
Animals with a deadly injury or defect, forbidden to eat

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: this is what it means:
provided that he does not compare in cases of treifos.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the ברייתא to one area
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to forbid comparing cases in all of Torah.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only forbids comparing cases of טריפות.

steps.title: A ברייתא: no comparing between טריפות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רב אשי: with טריפות you cannot say one case is like another, because a cut in one spot kills while a cut in another spot does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: with טריפות we do not say 'this one is like that one.' Don't be surprised, because you can cut an organ here and the animal dies, and cut it there and the animal lives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רב אשי said, and gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With טריפות, tiny differences in where an injury is decide whether the animal will live. So two injuries that look alike can have opposite results, and only the exact cases that were taught can be relied on.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
This one is like that one
And do not be surprised
One cuts it

steps.whyThisMatters: This is why the הלכות of טריפות are kept to the specific cases that were taught, and not stretched by comparison.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraisa:
With treifos, one does not say
"this one is like that one."
And do not be surprised,
for you can cut it from here and it dies,
cut it from here and it lives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב אשי's answer in step 13 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's claim that comparing is forbidden specifically with טריפות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that with טריפות one does not say one case is like another.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: don't act until I say it is for practice
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי asks רבי יוחנן whether they may act when he says 'this is the הלכה,' and רבי יוחנן says not until he says it is הלכה למעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said to רבי יוחנן: When you tell us 'the הלכה is like this,' may we act on it? He said: Do not act on it until I tell you it is the הלכה for practice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real exchange between a student and his teacher that shows the rule from step 10 in action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a teacher's own words 'this is the הלכה' were not enough to act on. Only when רבי יוחנן said explicitly 'הלכה למעשה' could the students rule in practice. This matches the ברייתא in step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: The master (a respectful way of saying 'you')
Should we act (on it in practice)?
The הלכה for actual practice

steps.whatToRemember: A stated הלכה, or even a case you saw, is not enough to rule from. You need to be told clearly it is הלכה למעשה, and even then you may not stretch it to cases of טריפות that only look similar.
steps.confusionAlert: 'הלכה הכי' and 'הלכה למעשה' sound almost the same, but here they are different. The first is a teaching, and only the second gives permission to act.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַסִּי לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said to Rabbi Yochanan:
When the master tells us "the halacha is like this,"
phrases.notes: "The master" is רבי יוחנן himself; רבי אסי is speaking to him politely.

phrases.english: should we act on it?
He said: Do not act
until I say "halacha for practice."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַסִּי לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the principle of steps 10-11 and shows it in a real exchange between a student and teacher.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not act on a teacher's statement 'this is the הלכה' until he explicitly says it is הלכה למעשה.

steps.title: רבא's instructions about finding a flaw in his rulings
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells his students not to cancel his ruling if they find a flaw. While he is alive they should ask him. After his death they should neither cancel it nor learn from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב פפא and to רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: When a written ruling of mine comes to you and you see a problem with it, do not tear it up until you come to me. If I have a reason, I will tell you; if not, I will take it back. After my death, do not tear it up, but also do not learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his students clear instructions on how to handle a ruling of his that seems wrong to them. He gives one rule for while he is alive and a different rule for after he dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While רבא is alive, the problem can be settled by asking him, so they must wait before canceling. After his death no one can ask him, so the ruling stays in an in-between state. It is not canceled, but no one relies on it for future cases.

keyTerms.meaning: A legal ruling, often written down for the people in the case
A refutation, a flaw or problem in the reasoning
You tear it up, meaning cancel the written ruling
I retract, I take back what I said
After death

steps.confusionAlert: After his death רבא does NOT say the ruling is canceled. He says two separate things: don't tear it up, AND don't learn from it. The ruling is left standing, but no one builds on it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This continues the earlier steps about when a ruling may be relied on. It shows that a great teacher's ruling should not be thrown out quickly, but also should not be followed blindly once a real flaw is seen.

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Pappa
and to Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אָתֵי פִּסְקָא דְּדִינָא דִּידִי לְקַמַּיְיכוּ,
phrases.english: When a legal ruling of mine comes before you,
and you see a refutation in it,
do not tear it up until you come before me;

phrases.aramaic: אִי אִית לִי טַעְמָא – אָמֵינָא לְכוּ,
phrases.english: if I have a reason, I will tell you,
and if not, I will retract.
After my death,
do not tear it up,
and also do not learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רָבָא לְרַב פָּפָּא וּלְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme from step 15 of when and how a teacher's ruling may be relied on in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: While רבא is alive, a ruling of his that seems flawed is not canceled until he is asked. After his death, it is neither canceled nor used as a basis for other rulings.

steps.title: Why the ruling should not be torn up after his death
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the first half of his after-death rule: don't cancel the ruling, because if he were there he might have given a good reason for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not tear it up, because if I had been there, perhaps I would have told you a reason.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now begins explaining his two after-death rules, starting with why the ruling should not be canceled. The explanation of the second rule comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The flaw the students see might not be a real flaw. רבא might have had a reason they did not think of, and since he can no longer explain it, they should not be sure enough to cancel the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, maybe
A reason, an explanation
There

phrases.english: Do not tear it up —
because if I had been there
perhaps I would have told you a reason;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the first after-death instruction in step 16, not to tear up the ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A flawed-looking ruling is not canceled after the teacher's death, because he might have had a valid reason that can no longer be heard.
